newsitem.title: FINLAND: Shares end ahead as upbeat Dow echoes in Helsinki.
newsitem.headline: Shares end ahead as upbeat Dow echoes in Helsinki.

text.p: Shares pushed ahead on Monday, bolstered by Wall Street's strong showing on Friday despite lingering fears of a U.S. rate hike, brokers said.
The HEX index closed up 1.17 percent at 2,116.39, in fair volume totalling 290 million markka; 29 percent of it in Nokia which closed official trade up 3.50 markka at 118.50.
"The firmer opening of the Dow helped to boost sentiment further and I expect to see more gains tomorrow," one said.
Food and biotech group Cultor was the latest of at least five companies in the past month or so to warn on its profit, and its stock took a 15 markka knock to 210.00.
But analysts were largely unfazed by the newest warning, saying the rash of downgrades did not look likely to amount to a bearish signal for the HEX index short-term.
Jaakko Niemela, analyst at Opstock securities, noted that many of the companies' earnings warnings had been clearly signalled in advance, and none came from major bourse engines.
Trade in Valmet was bolstered by news of its latest paper machine order to Japan, taking the share up one markka to 76.00.
But renewed profit-taking turned margarine maker Raision Tehtaat down four markka to 285.00.
